title: Rear Side Lamp Bulb Removal and Installation
introduction:
A small rear side lamp gets a backstage entrance: reach its connector and holder from underneath the raised vehicle, behind the rear bumper’s outer corner beside the exhaust and muffler shown in the drawing. I keep the electrical connector, twist-lock holder and bulb distinct—the holder is the little bayonet-style mount that must come out before the bulb can leave it.

Use the lamp illustrations to locate the work area and the lifting drawing to find the marked support locations. This guide covers removal and refitting; replacement-bulb specification and electrical fault diagnosis are outside its scope.

items.name: Prevent unexpected starting
items.detail: Before working around or underneath the vehicle, disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started at any time, causing personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine during service; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Use personal protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle, and protective gloves when handling sharp or pointed components. Failure to use the required protection may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Check capacity and lift locations
items.detail: Use a hoist with capacity sufficient for the vehicle’s weight, including cargo and modifications. Position its arms at the locations shown in the lifting overview. Locate the triangles stamped into the uni-body sheet metal or frame; the drawing’s circled areas and inset views help identify them. Lifting elsewhere may allow the vehicle to shift or fall, causing serious personal injury. Incorrect arm positioning can also cause unintended movement and serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Keep powered wheels clear
items.detail: Do not use the engine to power the drive wheels unless all drive wheels are elevated off the ground. Powered drive wheels contacting the ground can cause unintended vehicle movement, resulting in serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Check adapter and fork clearance
items.detail: Before lifting, position the hoist adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering-linkage components to prevent damage. On a two-column hoist, keep the forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped. Position the hoist to avoid damaging the axle or rear cover.

items.name: Check drive-on lift clearance
items.detail: If using a drive-on lift, check for underbody interference before driving onto it; interference may damage the underbody.

items.name: Protect the bumpers
items.detail: Never apply jack pressure to either bumper. Doing so will damage the bumper covers.

items.name: Use the required hoist for this procedure
items.detail: The vehicle’s supplied jack is intended only for an emergency deflated-tire change. Using it to raise the vehicle for another purpose may damage the vehicle.

items.name: If a jack is used during vehicle preparation
items.detail: Confirm that its capacity covers vehicle weight, cargo and modifications. Use the correct marked jacking points on a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block all wheels remaining on the ground. After jacking, support the vehicle with floor stands. Never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack: it can lower unexpectedly, and unintended movement can cause serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Before lifting and during lowering
items.detail: Start on a hard, level surface with the parking brake applied and wheels on the ground chocked. Keep the parking brake applied throughout this job. Establish secure support on the hoist before going underneath. Before lowering, clear tools and people from the lowering area and confirm the parking brake remains applied. On an arm-type hoist, restore wheel chocks as the tires reach the ground before withdrawing the arms; on a drive-on lift, retain wheel restraints through lowering.

requirements.category: Make sure the lamp is off

items.name: Before disconnecting the connector
items.detail: Select lamps off at the headlamp switch and visually confirm the rear side lamp is off before unplugging it. Autolamps can leave exterior lamps illuminated after ignition-off, so key removal alone does not confirm that the lamp has gone out.

edits.text: Raise the vehicle on a hoist positioned at the specified lifting points. Refer to: [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631) (100-02 Jacking and Lifting, Description and Operation).
edits.why: Access is from underneath the vehicle. I use the lifting overview’s inset views to match the stamped triangle locations to the actual body before the hoist takes the load.

edits.text: Unplug the electrical connector for the side lamp bulb at the highlighted location.
edits.why: This releases the wiring connection before the holder is turned. The vehicle inset locates the lamp area, and the close-up identifies the connector.

edits.text: Release and withdraw the bulb holder first, then remove the bulb from that extracted holder.
edits.why: The bulb stays in its holder while the holder comes out of the lamp. Once the holder is clear, take the bulb from its end as identified in the inset. The connector, holder and bulb are separate pieces of the sequence.

edits.text: Before taking out the bulb, turn the bulb holder counterclockwise and withdraw the holder from the lamp.
edits.why: Turning releases the holder’s twist-lock attachment. The larger illustration identifies the holder and its withdrawal direction.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: fit the bulb into its holder, insert the holder into the lamp and turn it clockwise to secure it, reconnect the electrical connector, then lower the vehicle from the hoist.
edits.why: The holder restores the bulb’s mechanical mounting, and reconnecting the plug restores its electrical connection. Clockwise refitting reverses the prescribed counterclockwise release. Before lowering, check the holder is retained, the connector is latched and the short lead follows its original route. Keep the parking brake and wheel restraints as described in preparation. Once the car is on the ground and restrained, use the headlamp switch to select the parking lamps and observe the repaired rear side lamp. Confirm it illuminates, then switch the lamps off. This ordinary completion check follows the [exterior lighting overview](#/document/G1694241); a lamp that remains dark needs fault diagnosis, not another guessed replacement.
